description: A web application where the core feature calls an LLM API. Examples: AI chatbot, document summarizer, code explainer, AI tutor clone, prompt-based content generator.

phases.core_concept: Three-tier architecture — why every AI app is frontend, your backend, then the LLM API, and what each tier is responsible for in [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the initial project scaffold (folder structure, .gitignore, README outline)
Generate a requirements.txt / dependency list for the chosen stack
human_required_tasks: Draw the three-tier architecture for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]: frontend, your backend, the LLM API — and mark where the API key lives. NOTE: The key lives in your backend only. If your diagram shows the frontend talking to the LLM API directly, you are doing it wrong.
Define the core user loop in one paragraph: what the user does, what your backend does, what the LLM returns
Create the .env file locally and confirm it is listed in .gitignore before the first commit
explanation_gate_targets: Why the frontend cannot call the LLM API directly, and what specifically someone could do if it did
What each of the three tiers is responsible for in [PROJECT_PURPOSE], in your own words
The exact path one user request takes through your planned system, from click to rendered response
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured environment setup script (venv, dependencies, .env template) — skip the manual setup walkthrough at the start of Phase 2

phases.core_concept: How a FastAPI backend is structured — routes, request/response models, startup config validation, and why all external calls live in a service layer instead of route handlers
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate FastAPI route boilerplate once the endpoint surface is decided
Generate Pydantic model stubs from your request/response field list
human_required_tasks: Decide the endpoint surface: which routes exist, their methods, and their request/response shapes for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
Write the config module that loads and validates every environment variable at startup
Decide what belongs in the service layer versus route handlers, and why
explanation_gate_targets: Why you chose these specific endpoints and request/response shapes for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
What happens, step by step, when a request arrives at your API with an invalid payload
Why environment variables are validated at startup instead of at first use, in your config module
Why LLM calls will live in a service module instead of inside route handlers in your project
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured FastAPI project skeleton with config validation and CORS wired — skip the configuration walkthrough in Phase 3

phases.core_concept: How LLM APIs work — message structure, context windows, tokens, and statelessness
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate error handling for rate limits and timeouts
human_required_tasks: Write the system prompt for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]. NOTE: This call must happen in your backend. If you are writing this in frontend code you are doing it wrong.
Design the conversation state management logic
Determine what context to include per call and why
explanation_gate_targets: Why the system prompt is structured the way it is for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
What happens to conversation history between calls
How token cost is calculated and why it matters for [PROJECT_SCALE]
Why a .env file in frontend code does not protect a secret
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Advanced: pre-built streaming response handler — skip manual implementation

phases.core_concept: Building a frontend that talks only to your backend — rendering untrusted AI and user content safely, and handling slow LLM responses gracefully
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the CSS layout and styling boilerplate
Generate a fetch wrapper with error handling once the endpoint contract is decided
human_required_tasks: Write the rendering logic for user and AI messages. NOTE: Every piece of user or AI content must be escaped or safely inserted (textContent, not innerHTML) — this is exactly where injection happens.
Design the loading, error, and empty states for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
Decide how the frontend tracks conversation state between messages
explanation_gate_targets: What specifically breaks if you render AI or user content with innerHTML without escaping, in your UI
How your frontend knows about and calls your backend — and why no key or secret appears anywhere in frontend code
What the user sees in your app while the LLM is generating a response, and how you built that
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-built chat interface component styled for your project — skip the message-list markup and scroll handling

phases.core_concept: Server-side authentication — Supabase Auth, JWT verification middleware, and why the API layer is the only place where auth actually counts
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate signup/login form markup and the client-side Supabase Auth calls
Generate the middleware boilerplate once the verification logic is decided
human_required_tasks: Write the auth verification middleware and attach it to every route that touches user data. NOTE: Hiding this in the UI does not protect it. This check must happen here, in the backend, on every request.
Decide which endpoints are protected and what each returns for unauthenticated (401) versus wrong-user (403 or 404) requests
Trace a JWT from login to a verified backend request in your app, and write down each step
explanation_gate_targets: What happens if the auth middleware is removed from one route in your backend — who can then do what
Why hiding the chat page behind a login redirect does not protect your API
How a token from your login flow gets verified in your middleware, step by step
When your API returns 401 versus 403, with a concrete example from your own endpoints
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Your explanation of the authentication architecture was thorough enough to skip the basic session setup walkthrough in Phase 6 — here's the pre-configured session handler. Plug it in and move straight to the logic layer.

phases.core_concept: Storing user data in Supabase — Row Level Security as the first line of defense, ownership policies, and parameterized access
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate typed query functions for your schema once tables and policies exist
human_required_tasks: Enable RLS on this table and write an ownership policy before continuing. Do not proceed until this is done.
Design the schema for conversations and messages, with a user_id ownership column on every table
Validate every user input that reaches the database and use parameterized queries — never string concatenation
explanation_gate_targets: What your RLS policy actually enforces, and why 'user is logged in' is not sufficient — ownership must be verified
What happens if the ownership check were removed — what anyone holding your public anon key could read or write
What breaks if input validation is removed from your message-save path
How your schema maps conversations to users, and what enforces that mapping
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Based on how you explained your database schema, you've unlocked the advanced query builder — a set of pre-written complex queries for your specific schema that would have taken manual work this phase

phases.core_concept: Verification, not learning — confirming against your actual running app that every security constraint you built is really enforced before you ship
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate a search script for secret patterns (api_key, secret, sk_live, token, password) across the codebase
human_required_tasks: Search the entire codebase for api_key, secret, sk_live, token, password. Confirm none appear in any frontend file or any file committed to the public repo.
Open browser DevTools Network tab. Make requests in the app. Confirm no secrets appear in any request or response payload.
Confirm all external API calls with secrets are made from backend functions, not frontend code.
Open Supabase Authentication → Policies. Confirm RLS is enabled on every table. Confirm every policy checks ownership, not just login status.
Attempt to access a protected route directly via URL or curl without being logged in. Confirm it returns 401, not data.
Attempt to access another user's data by manipulating a resource ID in a request. Confirm it returns 403 or 404, not the other user's data.
Confirm every user input that reaches the database uses parameterized queries, not string concatenation.
Confirm every user input that gets rendered in the UI is sanitized or escaped before rendering.
Run the app URL with /api, /admin, /dashboard, and other common paths appended. Document what responds and confirm nothing sensitive is exposed unintentionally.
explanation_gate_targets: Walk me through one item on this checklist. Tell me what you checked, what you found, and what you did or confirmed as a result.
Which checklist item surprised you or failed on first check in your app, and what you changed
Which single checklist item would be most damaging to skip for [PROJECT_PURPOSE], and what a stranger could do if you had skipped it
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Your gate scores across this project qualify you for the system design review — a full written architectural critique of your codebase you can reference in interviews
